cohort: 879 obstetrical patients with vulvodynia or vaginismus identified from a cohort of 13,792,544 patients admitted for delivery in US hospitals between 1999 and 2015
finding: Vulvodynia and vaginismus were associated with an increased risk of various maternal and neonatal morbidities, including eclampsia, chorioamnionitis, post-term pregnancy, cesarean delivery, and congenital anomalies.
mod_finding: Vulvodynia and vaginismus were associated with increased risks of cesarean delivery and instrumental vaginal delivery.
